message.content:
Answer: D
Reason: Malignant mesothelioma typically presents as a pleural-based mass (homogenous opacity with an obtuse angle to the chest wall) and is strongly associated with asbestos exposure, evidenced by pleural calcifications (plaques), along with nodular pleural thickening. The CT images show a large pleural mass and calcified pleural plaques, supporting this diagnosis over others like lung parenchymal tumors (which would have air bronchograms or acute angles).
